result.topic: Audit of the shared backtest harness (deep/harness.py v1) and the audited harness_v2
result.summary:
I audited the shared backtest harness that every research family relies on. The cost model is correct, and the decision path has no look-ahead leak for signals that only look at their own pair. But I found realism and survivorship bugs that change some of the established facts. All confirmed bugs are fixed in audit/harness_v2.py, which has the same API, uses the same series.pkl cache and needs no rebuild.

Writing REPORT.md was blocked by the harness (subagents must return findings as text), so the full report is in the findings and recommendations below.

**Look-ahead tests (passed for per-pair signals):**
- Brute-force checks of P(), ago and window: 0 mismatches.
- The ticker index used by the rug screen: 0 mismatches.
- A "poisoned future" test, where every value after a cut time T* is scrambled: decisions, exit_fn calls and trades closed before T* were identical.
- Two leaks do exist, both fixed in v2:
  - `P.static('price')` returns the whole column, future included.
  - simulate runs pair by pair, so any state a signal keeps across pairs sees other pairs' future (118,272 of 130,986 calls came after a call at a later time).

**Cost model:** identical to the engine's `paper_market_feasibility.modeled_roundtrip` on 135,512 raw rows (0 differences, 0 fee-tier mismatches).

**Main realism bug: stale fills.** The `upd` column is the engine's batch time (37,771 distinct values over 3.1M rows), not DexScreener's per-pair update time. The engine polls every ~5 s, but DexScreener refreshes a pair only every ~30 s, so 90% of kept points repeat the previous price exactly. v1 therefore filled entries at the signal's own price 86-89% of the time and exits at the trigger price 94-96% of the time. That means zero effective latency, and one take-profit filled at +432% on a single-print spike.
- Against the on-chain tape, DexScreener's price is the last trade from about 20 s earlier. It also bounces about ±50 bps between buy and sell prints.
- v2 fills at the next DexScreener refresh (the first later point whose price differs, within 60 s). Fill error against the tape drops from 188 to 114 bps, and most of the context-dependent bias disappears.

**Survivorship in forward_net.** It silently dropped samples whose pair left the feed (13.5% of 60-minute samples, mostly drained pools). Fact #1's 60-minute numbers change as follows:
- fee100-125 & liq>=250k: **+7.69% becomes -46.1%** (sample count 333 becomes 706).
- fee<=50 & liq>=250k: -0.49% becomes -4.04%.
- fee100-125 & liq50-250k: +0.47% becomes -5.18%.

**Fact #2 (random entries lose) stands under v2.** Holdout mean per trade at the stressed basis:

| universe | v1 | v2 |
|---|---|---|
| all PumpSwap | -7.68% | -7.20% |
| cost-first | -5.97% | -5.59% |
| cost-first + interim rug guard | -3.30% | -2.98% |

The rug guard's benefit is overstated. Its thresholds were chosen after seeing 7 rugs that drained in the holdout window. A guard built only from the 3 train-window rugs gives -4.61% instead of -2.98%.

**smoke3.py run unchanged under each harness:**

| run | v1 train / holdout | v2 train / holdout |
|---|---|---|
| no guard | -3.68 / -5.97 | -3.32 / -5.59 |
| interim guard | -4.78 / -3.30 | -2.24 / -2.98 |

None of the momentum or dip probes or the random baselines is near positive expectancy under either harness.

**The candidate gate is far too weak for 22.8 hours of data.**
- The smallest effect the holdout can reliably detect is 2-3.5% per trade.
- With 20 holdout trades, a config whose true mean is -1% shows a positive holdout mean about 34% of the time.
- When 3 configs are picked on train, roughly 70% of families would show at least one false candidate.

Credible claims need about 240-800 holdout trades for a +2%/trade edge, which means 1-3 more days of data.

findings.title: Stale-quote fills: entries and exits filled at the decision price (zero effective latency)
findings.detail:
Cause:
- `upd` is the engine batch time (37,771 distinct values over 3.1M rows, ~82 rows each; t-upd median 1.2 s), not DexScreener's updatedAt.
- So the de-dup rule keeps one row per ~5 s scan. 89.3% of kept PumpSwap points repeat the previous price and 86.8% repeat price+liq+v5+mcap. Only 20k of 715k same-price rows carry new verified-flow data.
- DexScreener changes price every ~30 s (between changes: p10 26.5 s, p50 31.9 s, p90 68 s).

Effect in v1:
- Entry at i+1 had the same price as the signal 86-89% of the time.
- Exit at k+1 had the trigger's price 94-96% of the time, so gap risk was barely modeled.
- TP fills reached +432% on single prints. HOLD exits overshot by up to 87.5 min (p90 18.9 min).

Tape (113 pools, mid = sqrt(last buy x last sell)):
- Fill MAE vs truth at decision+2 s: v1 188 bps; v2 next-refresh rule 114 bps.
- Conditional mean bias after a >2% DexScreener up-move: v1 -66 bps (fill too high), v2 -6. After a >2% down-move: v1 +15 (median +26), v2 -12.
- Trade level, v1: STOP exits -0.6..-1.5% pessimistic; TP exits +0.3..+4.8% optimistic.

Fixed in v2 (F1): fill at the first later point whose price differs, within 60 s, else i+1. Afterwards the trigger->fill gap is p50 25-30 s, HOLD overshoot p90 0.7-0.8 min, and max TP fill +27.9%. Impact on config holdout means: -0.9..+1.1%/trade.

findings.title: forward_net survivorship bias inflated base rates (established fact #1 is wrong in several buckets)
findings.detail:
- v1 returned None when the pair had no point after the horizon although the dataset continued: 8,307 of 61,475 60-min samples (13.5%).
- Of 1,549 PumpSwap pairs, 1,470 leave the feed more than 10 min before the end. Their last liquidity is p10 $20, median $20k, so many were drained.
- v2 (F3) values them at last price -10% (VANISHED) or by the gap rule. It returns None only when right-censored at the dataset end.

60-min forward net, v1 -> v2:
- fee100-125 & liq>=250k: +7.69% (n 333, win 74.8%) -> -46.11% (n 706, median -13.4, p10 -100%)
- fee<=50 & liq>=250k: -0.49 -> -4.04 (median 0.01 -> -0.46)
- fee100-125 & liq50-250k: +0.47 -> -5.18
- fee100-125 & liq<50k: -14.55 -> -21.00
- fee55-95 & liq50-250k: -4.03 -> -5.58
- fee55-95 & liq>=250k: -2.95 -> -3.08

Survivorship plus the liq==0 fix alone (v1 fills) gives -46.15 for the first bucket, so the change is survivorship, not the fill rule.

findings.title: Candidate gate (holdout n>=20, mean>0) is statistically meaningless on 22.8 h
findings.detail:
Inputs:
- Per-trade stressed sd: 9.1% (mid-fee random) to 13.2% (all PumpSwap random).
- Pair-cluster design effect: 0.7-2.4.
- Minimum detectable effect at 80% power, holdout: 2.0-3.6% per trade.

False-pass risk under a true mean of -1% (sd 9%, design effect 1.5):
- P(holdout mean > 0) = 34% at n=20, 26% at n=50, 13% at n=150.
- With 3 configs pre-selected on train, P(at least one false pass) = 72% / 60% / 35%.

Holdout trades needed for 80% power: +3%/trade 106-353; +2% 238-795; +1% 950-3,200.

The span is one 22.8 h regime; train and holdout cover different times of day. Random all-PumpSwap hourly means range from -15.6% to -2.9%. 3.2% of train trades exit after the cut (no embargo).

This cannot be fixed in code; see recommendations.

findings.title: Cross-pair look-ahead: pair-by-pair simulate lets global state in signal/exit_fn see other pairs' future
findings.detail:
- v1: 118,272 of 130,986 signal calls happened after a call at a later time. Any cross-sectional or regime state kept inside a signal is leaky.
- v2 (F5): a heap scheduler over per-pair generators invokes every callback (signal, size_fn, exit_fn) in global non-decreasing time order.
- Result: 0 inversions. Trades are identical to pair order for stateless signals (3 configs verified). About 25% slower.
- Custom `run(H)` simulators must enforce time order themselves.

findings.title: Past.static() leaks the full future column
findings.detail:
- v1 `P.static('price')` returned the whole array, so `P.static('price')[P.i+1]` was possible.
- v2 (F4) raises LookAhead for any time-series column. Static keys (pair, mint, dex, quote_sol, sym, created) still work.
- `P.s` remains reachable in Python. Integrators should grep strategy modules for `P.s[`, `.s['` and `P.i +`.

findings.title: Feed gaps while holding: exit at reappearance price, hold limits overshot, tails selected
findings.detail:
v1 behavior:
- 66 of 1,057 random trades sat through a >5 min feed absence (gap median 53 min, p90 111 min). They exited at the reappearance price, and stops/targets could not act during the gap.
- Those trades averaged +2.16% vs -9.68% for the others.

Gap returns vs matched continuously observed controls over the same interval:
- median +0.5% vs 0.0%
- p90 +25% vs +7.6%
- share below -50%: 4.8% vs 2.2%
- liq>=250k gaps: +1.4% median, no drains

v2 (F2):
- Absence over 10 min closes the trade, valued at min(pre-gap, return price). This is conservative: drains during a gap are kept and re-listing pumps are not credited.
- exit_t = return time (when the value is known). An earlier variant stamped the pre-gap time, and the poisoned-future test caught it.
- No extra haircut (GAP_HAIRCUT_PCT=0). Switches: GAP_VALUATION 'pre'/'return', FEED_GAP_MS=None.

Impact: -1.2..+0.7%/trade with no consistent sign; 6-17% of trades become FEED_GAP/GAP.

findings.title: Interim rug screen thresholds were fit using holdout rugs
findings.detail:
- All 10 drained cost-first pools are flagged at their first cost-first point, but 7 of the 10 drained in the holdout window.
- DAWS ($22.9M market cap, liq/mcap 1.89%, no ticker reuse, holdout drain) sits just inside the $20M / 2% thresholds.
- The 3 train-window rugs (IOF x2, SARP) had mcap $242-853M, liq/mcap 0.31-0.58%, and all reused a ticker.
- v2 keeps interim_rug_risk unchanged (shared API) and adds rug_risk_train_only(P): mcap >= $200M & liq/mcap < 1% & young, or young + ticker reuse.
- Random cost-first holdout: interim guard -2.98% vs train-only guard -4.61% (v2); v1 -3.30% vs -4.98%. About 1.6%/trade of the guard's holdout benefit is holdout-informed.

findings.title: (pair, hour) cluster bootstrap CI is about as narrow as iid
findings.detail:
- Trades on the same token are correlated across hours.
- Pair-level design effect: 1.98 (train) and 2.37 (holdout) for random all-PumpSwap.
- So (pair, hour) CIs are up to ~35% too narrow.
- v2 (F7) adds ci95_mean_usd_pair (bootstrap over pairs) and keeps the original field.

findings.title: DexScreener price is a ~20 s lagged last-trade print with bid/ask bounce
findings.detail:
- Best-lag match to the raw tape last trade is at a 20 s lag: median abs error 38 bps, vs 94 bps at lag 0.
- Same-second buy vs sell prints differ by a median of 106 bps, so the last-trade price bounces about ±50 bps.
- Trade-level path noise vs tape (mean abs difference per trade): 1.7-3.2%.
- Residual mean bias in v2: -0.6..+0.9%/trade. Dip-buying is still about +0.9% optimistic (n=42), comparable to the +50 bps/leg stress.
- This cannot be removed with DexScreener data. Strategies targeting moves of 3% or less over short holds are at the noise floor.

findings.title: Drained pools (liquidity == 0) valued at 80% of price
findings.detail:
- 570 PumpSwap points have liq == 0, and all are terminal (drained pools).
- v1 exit_value applied the 20% impact cap there, crediting 80% of the price.
- v2 (F6) values them at 0.
- Affected 8 of 1,652 trades in the 3 regression configs (all differences explained).

findings.title: portfolio() allowed negative balance and drawdown above 100%
findings.detail:
- v1 example: tight momentum probe final balance -437.46, max drawdown 143.75%.
- v2 portfolio is cash-limited: a trade is taken only if realized cash minus committed capital covers its size. It reports skipped_no_cash.
- Same results on the hand-checked examples (slot skip; drawdown 1.98%).

findings.title: summarize edge cases: upper median and trades_per_hour span
findings.detail:
- median_pct used the upper median for even n (n=2 example: 2.5 instead of 1.0).
- trades_per_hour used the first-to-last entry span instead of the evaluated window.
- Both fixed in v2. Summaries also add censored_end, vanished and gap_closed counts.

findings.title: END censoring and VANISHED haircut are assumptions
findings.detail:
END censoring:
- Entries in the last hour are marked to market at the final price.
- Excluding entries in the last 65 min changes holdout means by -0.05..-0.24%. Kept, with a count reported.

VANISHED -10% haircut:
- Kept. Tape evidence is thin: 20 vanished pools still traded afterwards, price at +10 min mean -14.2%, median +0.9%, p10 -70.7%.
- 232 of 252 vanished tape pools have no later swaps.

findings.title: load() would silently rebuild the shared cache
findings.detail:
- v1 load() calls build_cache() and overwrites series.pkl if it is missing.
- v2 never auto-builds; build_cache(path) requires an explicit path. The cache was not rebuilt.

findings.title: Verified correct: cost model, Past view bounds, ticker index, net50 path, cooldown, de-dup ordering
findings.detail:
Cost model:
- Fee tier from mcap / (price/pnative), using the engine's PUMP_FEE_TIERS. The engine's marketCap-or-fdv fallback never triggered in the data.
- Impact 2N/L is exact for constant-product buys and conservative for sells up to the 20% cap.
- 20 bps buffer per leg; network fee on both legs as in the engine.
- net50 re-prices qty50 at the same fill and exit.

Mechanics:
- No overlaps or cooldown violations (2,959 random trades).
- Out-of-order rows via the 15 s rule: 71 (negligible).
- A-B-A price flip-flops: 5% of changes, 0.3% within 15 s (bounce, not multi-writer echoes).

Open question: same-second buy/sell spread ~106 bps on pools with a modeled 100 bps fee. The decoded quote amounts may exclude part of the fee. Not acted on.

Housekeeping: tape_snapshot.sqlite3-shm/-wal in deep/ predate my first tape access (WAL file created 10:41:15, my first tape script 10:43). The main DB is unmodified (mtime 10:31).

findings.title: v1 vs v2 results (stressed net50 mean % per trade, train(n) / holdout(n), -5/+10/60 unless noted)
findings.detail:
| config | v1 train (n) | v1 holdout (n) | v2 train (n) | v2 holdout (n) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| smoke3 random cost-first, no guard | -3.68 (83) | -5.97 (129) | -3.32 (84) | -5.59 (126) |
| smoke3 cost-first + interim guard | -4.78 (27) | -3.30 (43) | -2.24 (28) | -2.98 (40) |
| cost-first + train-only guard | -4.65 | -4.98 | -2.24 | -4.61 |
| random all PumpSwap | -9.94 (589) | -7.68 (468) | -11.10 (579) | -7.20 (468) |
| random fee 52.5-125 & liq>=50k + guard | -4.48 | -4.32 | -5.57 | -4.69 |
| momentum +3%/60 s probe | -6.15 | -4.17 | -5.38 | -5.28 |
| dip -3%/60 s probe | -3.81 | -4.79 | -5.69 | -4.12 |
| momentum -3/+3/15 | -4.74 | -3.68 | -4.30 | -3.45 |

Per-fix decomposition and gap-valuation sensitivity: audit/t12_compare.out and t12_compare.json.

Holdout portfolio (3 slots), cost-first + guard: v1 764.78 / 23.5% drawdown; v2 795.20 / 20.5%.

Regression checks:
- v2 in v1 mode reproduces v1 exactly except the 8 liq==0 trades.
- Time-ordered equals pair-ordered for all 3 configs.
- forward_net parity: 5 mismatches out of 14,837.

recommendations: Re-run every family's strategies.py under v2 before accepting anything: `python audit/rerun_with_v2.py <family>/strategies.py --v1-too` (it aliases `harness` to v2, so modules run unchanged). Report v2 stressed results as primary.

Revise established fact #1. Under v2, 60-min base rates are fee100-125 & liq>=250k -46.1% (not +7.69%), fee<=50 & liq>=250k -4.04% (not -0.49%), fee100-125 & liq50-250k -5.18%. The old numbers came from survivorship. Flag fact #3's screen as holdout-informed: also report results with `rug_risk_train_only`, where random cost-first holdout is -4.61% vs -2.98% with the interim guard.

Tighten the candidate gate. Replace holdout n >= 20 / mean > 0 with: holdout n >= 150 across >= 25 pairs; pair-level CI95 lower bound of mean net50 > 0 (`ci95_mean_usd_pair`); beating the same-period random baseline by more than its CI half-width; positive under `rug_risk_train_only`, `GAP_VALUATION='pre'` and `'return'`, and `FILL_RULE='next_point'`; top_pair_share <= 0.2. Treat anything weaker as a hypothesis for forward paper testing.

Collect more data before claiming any edge. A +2%/trade edge needs about 240-800 holdout trades (1-3 more days of scan log); +1% needs about 1,000-3,200. Re-validate any survivor walk-forward on days after 2026-10-08 10:27, with no re-tuning.

Strategy authors should use time-based `P.ago`/`P.window`, not `back=k` (k points are about k/6 distinct DexScreener updates). They should treat moves under ~1% within 30 s as bid/ask bounce, and avoid targets of 3% or less: the per-trade DexScreener-vs-chain noise is 1.7-3.2%.

Integrator: grep strategy modules for `P.s[`, `.s['`, `P.i +` and module-level state mutated inside signals. Make sure custom `run(H)` simulators process events in global time order; v2's `simulate` already does.

Live engine (outside this research): DexScreener data refreshes only every ~30 s and lags the chain by ~20 s. Any paper fill priced at the DexScreener quote at decision time is optimistic for take-profit exits and dip entries. Using the on-chain tape or a route quote for fills would make PAPER PnL more honest.

result.topic: Rug/drain detector for the PumpSwap PAPER dataset (label: rug): rug_guard_v1, drain census, hazard by slice, engine-flag check, and corrections to shared facts
result.summary:
PAPER research only; nothing here is a profit claim. The rug guard works as a risk filter. No edge strategy came out of this study (0 candidates): random entries lose -3.8% to -5.0% per trade on holdout at net50 in every universe, with or without the guard. Thresholds were chosen on TRAIN only (configs_tried = 8,960 grid configurations), three configs were frozen before any holdout look (rug_guard.frozen.sha256), and holdout was evaluated once.

The harness blocked writing REPORT.md ("subagents should return findings as text"), so the report content is in these findings. All other deliverables are in the rug folder.

(a) DRAIN CENSUS
- 1,549 PumpSwap SOL-quote pools had 157 terminal drains in 22.8 h: 97 in the train period, 60 in holdout, plus 3 recovered glitches. 115 were fast (>= 80% within 10 min); 42 were slow collapses.
- Liquidity just before the drain: <$20k 90, $20-50k 30, $50-250k 18, >= $250k 19.
- Median pair age at drain: 12.8 min.
- All 19 drains in pools that ever had >= $250k liquidity belonged to two structural families:
  1. LP-PULLABLE (9 of the 19; 25 drains in total). liq/mcap 1.2-1.9 on non-pump mints with 115-125 bps fees. Liquidity goes to 0.0 at an unchanged price and the pool leaves the feed. Tickers are recycled heavily (TWEETCRAFT x3, SharkTank x4, BORDR, Anthropic, ...). Of the 30 such pools whose fate was observable, 24 were pulled within the 22.8 h.
  2. FAKE MARKET CAP (10). USDP/IOF/UDR/DOTF/GOIF/WSOS/VSOF/SARP/DAWS...: $23M-$1.3B 'market cap' on liq/mcap 0.25-1.9%, 0.3-4 days old.
- Every other drain hit a young pool.
- Tape: it decodes swaps only, so it cannot see LP removal. Family drains show NO sell burst (0 swaps in the 10 min before IOF/GOIF/DOTF drained). Their prior flow is almost only small buys (23:2, 63:1, 23:1). One seller wallet (4NA1SWzb) traded both GOIF and DOTF. Detection must therefore be structural, not flow-based.

(b) THE RULE: rug_guard_v1(P) -> True means do not trade. It blocks if ANY of:
- liq/mcap >= 1.0 (LP_PULLABLE)
- pair age < 720 min (YOUNG_POOL)
- mcap >= $20M AND liq/mcap < 1% AND age < 14 d (FAKE_MCAP)
- liquidity, market cap or age is missing or non-positive (fail closed).

HOLDOUT results (train in brackets):
- liq >= $20k: 89.7% of drain events flagged [0.891]; 87.2% flagged at every pre-drain point. Point recall 0.709, FPR 0.148 [0.224], precision 0.309, pool-averaged FPR 0.277.
- liq >= $50k: event recall 0.818 [0.810], FPR 0.139.
- Cost-first slice: event recall 0.857 [1.0], FPR 0.298. Those 'false positives' are fake-family pools still alive at the end or draining more than 2 h later.
- fee 100-125 & liq >= $50k: 0.857 [0.778], FPR 0.086.
- References: the INTERIM screen gets 0.718 at FPR 0.485 (its thresholds were set on the full data, so its holdout is contaminated). Young-only gets 0.744 but catches 0 of 7 cost-first drains. Structural-only (no age gate) gets 0.436.
- Holdout misses: DAWS (liq/mcap 1.86%, above the 1% threshold), OURA (3.65%, wash-traded), and two slow collapses of 1.3-day-old coins.
- A 2% FAKE threshold would also have caught DAWS. Train could not tell 1% from 2%, so that variant is holdout-informed and NOT validated.

(c) DRAIN HAZARD per position-hour (holdout, no guard -> rug_guard_v1, share of decision points kept)
| slice | no guard | rug_guard_v1 (kept) | interim screen (kept) |
|---|---|---|---|
| liq >= $20k | 4.39%/h | 1.31%/h (81%) | |
| cost-first: fee <= 50 & liq >= $250k | 3.48%/h | 0.99%/h (68%) | 0% (30%) |
| fee 100-125 & liq $50-250k | 3.45%/h | 0.21%/h (85%) | |
| fee 100-125 & liq >= $250k | 54%/h | blocked entirely | |
A drain costs about 100% of the position, so the guard removes roughly 3 percentage points of expected loss per position-hour.

(d) ENGINE FLAGS
- Fake family: rows carry 'unnatural buy imbalance' 61% of the time and 'weak liquidity/MC' 93% (mean score 49, posture WAIT 91%). But these are only score penalties, they also fire on legitimate pools, and they have no lift on their own.
- LP family: the engine gives the +9 'good liquidity/MC' bonus on 98.6% of rows (mean score 86.7, posture SETUP 96.9%). Only the winner_signal and flow-unavailable gates kept it out.
- safety.allowed=false on family rows means the check never ran (checked_at 0), not that it blocked them.

CORRECTIONS TO SHARED FACTS AND TOOLS
1. Fact 1's +7.69%/60m (win 74.8%) for fee 100-125 & liq >= $250k is survivorship bias. H.forward_net dropped 375 of 708 samples whose pair ended before the horizon. Including them: mean -46.2%, median -13.9%, p10 -100%. The cost-first base rate also moves from -0.49% to -3.52%. Its 50% win rate was the fake family's wash-buy drift; with the guard the win rate is 24.6% and the median -0.89%.
2. H.exit_value caps impact at 20% and books zero liquidity as 20% impact. An LP pull therefore costs about -22..-32% in the harness instead of ~-100%. In the fee >= 100 & liq >= $250k universe, harness -3.6..-6.7% per trade becomes -17.8..-23.3% with an uncapped exit (realistic_exit.py).

FORWARD CHECK
On 36.5 min of observations logged after the cutoff (read-only): 4 drains, all under $20k and all flagged at every pre-drain point. No family pool drained in that window, which is too short for precision.

HOUSEKEEPING
An early stray 'python3' call (Windows Store alias) hung as a background shell job. I did not kill any process; the harness terminates it at turn end.

findings.title: Fact 1's only positive base rate is survivorship bias (forward_net drops drained pools)
findings.detail: fee100-125 & liq>=250k: forward_net-only n=333 mean +7.69% win 74.8% (reproduces fact 1). 375 of 708 one-per-minute samples were dropped because the pair series ended before +60 min. Keeping them, valued at the last point with an uncapped constant-product exit and the -10% vanish haircut: mean -46.15%, median -13.85%, p10 -100%. That slice is the LP-pull family; its measured drain hazard is 51.6%/position-hour (holdout 54%). The bias also inflates other slices: cost-first -0.49 -> -3.52 (768 ended samples), fee100-125 liq50-250k +0.47 -> -1.60, fee100-125 liq<50k -14.55 -> -20.56. Any study that ranks slices or signals by H.forward_net is affected. Script: rug/survivorship_all.py.

findings.title: Harness under-prices LP pulls: impact cap 20% and liq=0 booked as 20%
findings.detail: H.exit_value uses min(20%, 2N/L), and 20% when L<=0. When liquidity goes to 0.0 at an unchanged price (LP pull), the harness books about -22..-32% (STOP fill plus VANISHED -10%) instead of ~-100%. Random entries in fee>=100 & liq>=250k: harness mean -6.65% (train) / -3.64% (holdout) vs -23.3% / -17.8% with an uncapped exit, impact = max(min(x,0.2), x/(1+x)), x=2N/L, which equals the harness for x<=0.2. The integrator should re-value trades with rug/realistic_exit.revalue() or fix the audited harness.

findings.title: All 19 drains in big pools (>= $250k liquidity) came from two structural families
findings.detail: 157 terminal drains in 1,549 PumpSwap SOL pools in 22.8 h; 115 were fast (<= 10 min). The 19 drains in pools that ever had >= $250k liquidity: 9 LP_PULLABLE and 10 FAKE_MCAP. (1) LP_PULLABLE: liq/mcap 1.2-1.9 on non-pump mints, fee 115-125 bps, liquidity -> 0 at an unchanged price, recycled tickers (TWEETCRAFT x3, SharkTank x4, BORDR, Anthropic, SpaceX, XP, TITS, knightcat). 233 pools showed the signature at >= $20k; of the 30 with an observable fate, 24 were pulled and 4 were alive at the end; 203 were seen for about 1 min (fate unknown). (2) FAKE_MCAP: USDP/IOF/UDR/DOTF/GOIF/WSOS/VSOF/SARP/XRPN/ATFS/DAWS, $23M-$1.3B market cap on liq/mcap 0.25-1.9%, 0.3-4 days old. The other 138 drains were young pools: median age at drain 12.8 min, 104 under 60 min old.

findings.title: rug_guard_v1 holdout: 90% event recall at 15% point FPR (liq >= $20k)
findings.detail:
Rule: block if liq/mcap>=1.0, OR age<720 min, OR (mcap>=$20M AND liq/mcap<1% AND age<14d); fail closed on missing inputs. Chosen on train (8,960 configs, two passes) and frozen. HOLDOUT, train in brackets:
- liq>=$20k (39 events): event recall any 0.897 [0.891], all-points 0.872, point recall 0.709, FPR 0.148 [0.224], precision 0.309, pool-avg FPR 0.277.
- liq>=$50k (22): 0.818 [0.810], FPR 0.139.
- cost-first (7): 0.857 [1.0], FPR 0.298.
- fee100-125 & liq>=$50k (14): 0.857 [0.778], FPR 0.086.
- all PumpSwap (60): 0.933, FPR 0.147.
Comparison: INTERIM 0.718 at FPR 0.485 (contaminated); young-only 0.744 at FPR 0.052 but 0 of 7 cost-first drains; structural-only 0.436.
Misses: DAWS (liq/mcap 1.86%), OURA (3.65%, 12 wallets wash-trading), and slow collapses TON618 / AnyPS5.

findings.title: Drain hazard per position-hour falls ~3.4x with the guard
findings.detail:
HOLDOUT (share of decision points kept in brackets):
- all liq>=$20k: 4.39%/h -> 1.31%/h (81%); structural-only 2.36% (85%); interim 2.57% (49%).
- cost-first: 3.48% -> 0.99% (68%); interim 0.00% (30%).
- fee100-125 & liq$50-250k: 3.45% -> 0.21% (85%).
- fee100-125 & liq$20-50k: 16.5% -> 10.1% (70%).
- fee100-125 & liq>=$250k: 54% -> blocked entirely.
- fee55-95 & liq>=$250k: 0% (nothing blocked).
All data: liq>=$20k 4.28% -> 1.39% (78%); cost-first 3.22% -> 0.69% (59%). The remaining cost-first hazard is DAWS and 'D O T F' (liq/mcap 1.5-1.9%).

findings.title: Engine scoring rewards the LP-pull family; the safety check never ran on either family
findings.detail:
Recomputed from 2.2M raw rows.
- LP family: +9 'good liquidity/MC' on 98.6% of rows, mean score 86.7, posture SETUP on 96.9% of rows. Only winner_signal (31%) and promoted_verified_flow_unavailable (32%) rejections kept the engine out.
- Fake family: 'unnatural buy imbalance' (b5/s5>5) on 61% of rows and 'weak liquidity/MC' on 93% (score 49, WAIT 91%). These are score penalties only; they also fire on 42 of 71 legitimate train pools with >= $50k liquidity, and they have no lift on their own (2h drain rate 5.8% vs 4.7%).
- safety.allowed=false on 100% of family rows, but the raw rows show checked_at 0: the check was never run, so it did not block anything.
- RUG_GUARD_V2 (rugcheck) passed SharkTank 65GHmCby (LP 100% locked), which later collapsed.

findings.title: Tape shows no sell burst before family drains: detection must be structural
findings.detail: The tape snapshot decodes swaps only (no LP add/remove). IOF, GOIF and DOTF had 0 swaps in the 10 min before draining. Their prior 2h flow was almost only small buys of 0.1-0.2 SOL (buys:sells 23:2, 63:1, 23:1), the wash-buy pattern. One seller wallet (4NA1SWzb) traded both GOIF and DOTF. OURA had 292 swaps from 12 wallets. LP-pull pools show 0-2 swaps on the tape although DexScreener reported hundreds of transactions per 5 min (tape coverage may be incomplete). Young-pool dumps do show distributed selling (Bond: 71 sells / 11 buys in the final 10 min).

findings.title: Guard removes the catastrophic tail but creates no edge: 0 candidates
findings.detail:
Random entries, -5/+10/60, paired draws, HOLDOUT net50 (no guard -> guard):
- cost-first: -5.01% (n131, 27 pairs) -> -4.95% (n78, 13 pairs, PF 0.09, CI95 $[-17.6,-4.3], portfolio $674, maxDD 33%).
- liq>=$20k: -4.54% (n688) -> -4.18% (n515, 58 pairs, PF 0.21).
- fee>=100 & liq>=$50k: -3.73% (realistic -4.62%) -> -3.76% (n184, 15 pairs).
Trades worse than -50%, realistic exit, train+holdout: cost-first 8 -> 3, liq>=$20k 10 -> 1, fee>=100 & liq>=$50k 8 -> 0. No config meets holdout mean net50 > 0. The cost-first slice's 50% 60-min win rate was the fake family's wash-buy uptrend; with the guard it is 24.6% (median -0.89%).

findings.title: FAKE_MCAP threshold 1% vs 2%: tied on train; 2% would have caught DAWS on holdout (unvalidated)
findings.detail: Train could not separate 1% from 2% (same recall); 1% was taken for fewer flags. On holdout, DAWS ($23.8M market cap, 1.86%, 4.1 days, fast drain) slipped through at 1%. The 2% variant (the interim's value) is holdout-informed and has no clean out-of-sample estimate. Three live pools fit DAWS's profile and pass at 1%: USDF EpugLBw1, UDR ERFmQZQU, GOIF 8ZMkMgWM (market cap $21-32M, liq/mcap 1.6-2.0%, 4-8 days old, cost-first universe).

findings.title: Forward check on 36.5 min of post-cutoff observations
findings.detail: The engine's append-only observations log was read read-only from the dataset cutoff byte: 113 PumpSwap SOL pairs. 4 fast drains (CODY, CERT, Wick, PLAGUE), all under $20k and all flagged (YOUNG_POOL) at every pre-drain point. result.topic: calib: the harness cost model checked against real Jupiter quotes from 117 closed PAPER trades (ledger copies only), plus calibration.py
result.summary:
The harness gets the swap costs right, but it fills at a DexScreener price that lags the pool. So on real trades it was too optimistic by about 0.56–0.76% per trade. The +50 bps/leg stress covers that on average, but not per trade, and not on stop-loss exits.

REPORT.md was not written: the harness blocks subagents from writing .md report files, so the report is here and in the findings.

**Data (copies only; live ledgers never opened)**
- 31 account-ledger copies from the backup and archive folders, deduplicated by (account, trade id): 117 closed trades with entry, preflight buy/sell and exit quotes plus a market snapshot.
  - 92 trades are from before the reset (Oct 6–7, before the dataset starts); 25 are after it, where dataset prices exist.
  - Only 9 tokens, and 5 of them (CATCRAFT 39, swordinu 29, RARINU 19, A1 18, IRL 8) carry 113 trades. The 3 accounts mirror each other, so there are only 39 (pair, hour) clusters; every confidence interval is a cluster bootstrap.
  - Range covered: $12–200 per trade, trade size 0.009–0.25% of pool liquidity, liquidity $33k–465k (only 2 trades under $50k), fee tiers 30/60/75/90–120 bps.
- 162 strategy-lab $10 Jupiter price checks on 12 pools, compared with the lab's price, which matched the dataset price exactly.
- The on-chain swap tape was inconclusive and is not used: its decoder reports about half the fee, and a mid-price rebuilt from recent swaps lags.

**Method**
- Each trade's own snapshot (price, SOL/USD, market cap, liquidity) is run through formulas identical to the harness entry/exit cost functions.
- "Booked" means the raw Jupiter quote minus the engine's 10 bps/leg buffer, plus $0.03 network fee per leg and token-account rent counted as a loss.
- For the 25 post-reset trades, the harness version buys at the dataset price at the entry quote and sells at the first dataset point after the exit quote.
- Plus (+) means real cost is higher than the model.

**T1: Buy then immediate sell (no price move in between) — booked round trip minus harness round trip, %**

| Bucket | n | Mean | Median | p90 | CI95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| All | 117 | −0.27 | −0.15 | −0.01 | [−0.38, −0.18] |
| fee ≤50, liq ≥250k | 23 | −0.10 | −0.09 | +0.01 | |
| fee 55–95, liq 50–250k | 61 | −0.15 | | | |
| fee 100–125, liq 50–250k | 29 | −0.51 | | | [−0.80, −0.27] |
| liq <50k | 2 | −1.85 | | | |

- The +50 bps stress covers 100% of trades here.
- On the pool leg alone, half the buy/sell spread minus (fee + modeled price impact) is −0.03% mean (n=87). So the fee-tier table is right to about 0.1%.
- Jupiter's USDC→SOL rate differs from DexScreener's SOL/USD by only −0.04%.

**T2: Entry leg vs the price the harness would fill at — booked minus harness, % per leg**
- Fresh dataset price (post-reset, about 0.35 s old): fill +0.35 (CI −0.00..+0.80, p90 +1.51), preflight buy +0.34.
- The sell quoted at the same moment was 0.67% better than the model: the executable mid sat about 0.5% above the DexScreener price.
- Snapshot price (about 8 s old), all trades: +0.25 mean, +0.18 median.
- Lab $10 checks, in harness-equivalent terms: fee ≤50 +0.50, fee 55–95 +0.09, fee 100–125 −0.60.
- This is a lag tied to the trigger, not a fixed bias of one pool. On the same pool, entries paid above the price, emergency exits sold about 0.5% below it, and stop exits were about 2% below the next price.

**T3: Exit leg — booked minus harness, % per leg**

| Comparison | n | Mean | CI95 |
|---|---|---|---|
| vs harness next-point fill, all post-reset | 25 | +0.76 | [+0.12, +1.70] |
| … EXIT_IMPACT_EMERGENCY exits | 20 | +0.18 | |
| … STOP_LOSS exits | 3 | +1.97 | [+1.19, +2.75] |
| vs ledger price, older STOP exits | 30 | +3.78 | |
| vs ledger price, emergency exits | 42 | −0.03 | |

- The 43 STALE_MARKET_EXIT closes are excluded: their exit prices were stale by construction.

**T4: Whole trade — booked P&L minus harness P&L, % per trade**

| Comparison | n | Mean | Other |
|---|---|---|---|
| Post-reset, vs harness | 25 | −0.76 | CI [−1.25, −0.26], p10 −2.13 |
| Post-reset, vs harness +50 stress | 25 | +0.23 | CI [−0.27, +0.72]; 60% of trades covered |
| Non-stop exits, vs harness | 22 | −0.56 | about 28 bps per leg |
| Stop exits, vs harness +50 | 3 | −1.25 | not covered |
| Post-reset, vs calibrated harness | 25 | +0.04 | CI [−0.50, +0.52]; in-sample for fee ≤50 |

**Exit-impact emergency (V1) and quote gaps**
- It closed 36% of all trades and 83% of fee ≤50 trades, after a median hold of only 30–44 s.
- 14.5% of trades already met the emergency threshold with the sell quote taken at entry.
- Jupiter's reported price impact includes the pool fee: reported buy impact minus modeled pool impact averages +0.63%.
- At these exits, liquidity was unchanged and the realised exit cost was 0.78% against a model of 0.41%.
- These trades booked −2.14% on average, but only −0.41% beyond the entry-time round-trip cost. The rule mostly locked in the round-trip cost on quote noise.
- Buy vs sell price at the same moment: mean gap 1.82%, median 2.17%, which is the real round-trip spread. Reported sell impact minus buy impact: median +0.18, p90 +0.56.

**Calibration (calibration.py, version CALIB_V1)**
- `extra_bps_per_leg(fee_bps, liq_usd, notional_usd, basis='engine', conservative=True)`, applied to both legs:
  - fee ≤50: +22 bps (raw-quote basis +12).
  - fee 55–95 and 100–125: +10 bps floor. The measured estimates are −5 and −55, meaning the harness already over-costs these tiers.
  - Plus fixed engine costs: rent $0.185 per trade and +$0.018 network per leg, which is +5.5 bps/leg at $200 and +22 at $50.
  - Plus +25 bps/leg outside the measured range (liquidity <$50k or trade above 0.3% of liquidity). This is a prior, not a measurement.
- `exit_reason_extra_bps`: stop exits +200 bps (measured), trailing exits +100 bps (a prior).
- `calibrated_net_pct(trade)` re-prices a finished harness trade.
- On random-entry baselines (stop −5 / target +10 / 60 min), holdout mean per trade:

| Baseline | net50 | Calibrated |
|---|---|---|
| All PumpSwap | −7.68 | −8.45 (stop-heavy) |
| Cost-first universe + rug screen | −3.30 | −3.30 |

**Caveats**
- "Real" means Jupiter quotes plus the engine's simulated 250 ms delay, not on-chain fills. No MEV is included, and landing at the 1% slippage limit would add about 0.9% per round trip.
- The fresh-price evidence is essentially one pool (swordinu, fee 30).
- Nothing is measured for liquidity <$50k or trades above $200.

findings.title: The harness is optimistic per trade because it fills at a lagging DexScreener price
findings.detail: Post-reset trades (n=25, 12 clusters, mostly fee-30 pools around $450k liquidity) booked 0.76% per trade worse than a harness version using dataset prices (CI95 −1.25..−0.26, p10 −2.13). Non-stop exits alone: −0.56% (n=22, CI −1.14..−0.03), about 28 bps per leg. The cause is not the fee or impact model. The DexScreener price lags the pool in the direction of the recent move: signal entries paid +0.35% (fresh price, CI −0.00..+0.80, p90 +1.51) and +0.50% (lab $10 checks, fee ≤50) above the harness entry cost.

findings.title: Stop-loss exits are much worse than the harness's next-point fill; +50 bps stress does not cover them
findings.detail: With fresh prices, stop exits booked +1.97% per leg worse than the harness's next-point fill (n=3, CI +1.19..+2.75). On 30 older trades the gap was +3.78% against ledger prices, which were partly stale. Whole-trade stop gap after the +50 stress was still −1.25%. calibration.exit_reason_extra_bps('STOP') = 200 bps. The fresh-price sample is tiny (n=3).

findings.title: EXIT_IMPACT_EMERGENCY V1 mostly fired on quote noise
findings.detail: It closed 42/117 trades (35.9%), 19/23 (82.6%) of fee ≤50 trades, and 38.7% of fee 100–125 trades, after a median hold of 30 s (44 s for fee ≤50). 14.5% of trades already met the threshold, max(0.75, entry impact + 0.5), with the sell quote taken at entry. Jupiter's priceImpactPct includes the pool fee: reported buy impact minus 2N/L = +0.63% mean. Fee-30 pools showed a median sell impact of 0.59% against the 0.75% floor. At these exits liquidity was unchanged (exit/entry 1.003) and the realised exit cost was 0.78% against a model of 0.41%. The trades booked −2.14% on average, of which only −0.41% (CI −0.89..+0.05) went beyond the entry-time round trip. The rule mostly locked in the round-trip spread.

findings.title: Fee tiers and the 2N/L impact formula are right or slightly conservative
findings.detail:
Buy then immediate sell (no price move between), booked round trip minus harness round trip:
- All 117 trades: −0.27% (median −0.15, p90 −0.01, CI −0.38..−0.18).
- fee ≤50 / liq ≥250k: −0.10.
- fee 55–95 / liq 50–250k: −0.15.
- fee 100–125 / liq 50–250k: −0.51 (CI −0.80..−0.27).
- liq <50k: −1.85 (n=2).

On the pool leg alone, half the buy/sell spread minus (fee tier + 2N/L) averaged −0.03% (median +0.07, n=87). Jupiter's USDC/SOL rate differs from DexScreener's SOL/USD by only −0.04%. The +50 bps/leg stress covers 100% of these round trips.

findings.title: +50 bps/leg stress covers the average gap but not individual trades
findings.detail: Post-reset whole trades minus the harness with +50 stress: +0.23% mean (CI −0.27..+0.72), median +0.41, p10 −1.16. Only 60% of individual trades were covered. Entry legs were covered in 52–62% of trades. Exit-impact-emergency exits were covered on average. Stop exits were not covered.

findings.title: The engine books fixed costs the harness omits
findings.detail: Token-account rent of about $0.185 is booked as a loss per trade (it is refundable on-chain), and the engine charges $0.03 network per leg against the harness's 0.0001 SOL (about $0.012). Together that is 5.5 bps per leg at $200 and 22 bps per leg at $50. calibration.fixed_engine_bps_per_leg(notional) models it (engine basis only).

findings.title: Booked costs assume quotes, not landed swaps
findings.detail: The engine books the expected quote minus 10 bps, after a simulated 250 ms delay. Its worst-case round trip at the 1% slippage floor averaged 3.07% versus 2.19% expected. Real swaps landing near the floor, or hit by MEV, would cost about 0.9% more per round trip; neither the engine nor this calibration includes that.

findings.title: Evidence is narrow; some data was excluded or inconclusive
findings.detail:
- 113 of 117 trades are on 5 tokens, and the fresh-price evidence is essentially one pool (swordinu, fee 30).
- The 43 STALE_MARKET_EXIT closes used stale pinned prices (the bug fixed in 566e941) and are excluded from the exit numbers.
- Older snapshot prices were about 8 s old.
- Nothing was measured for liquidity <$50k (n=2), trade size above 0.25% of liquidity, or trades above $200.
- The tape cross-check (22k points, 178 pools) was inconclusive: its half-spread was about fee/2 because of the decoder's fee accounting, and the mid rebuilt from recent swaps lags. It is not used.
- REPORT.md could not be written because the harness blocks subagents from writing report .md files; the content is in this output.

recommendations: Keep net50 (+50 bps per leg) as the acceptance basis. Also re-price every candidate with calibration.calibrated_net_pct and reject any config whose holdout mean is negative on that basis. Exact form: add extra_bps_per_leg(H.fee_bps(s,j), liq, size) on both legs, plus exit_reason_extra_bps(reason) on the exit leg.

Penalise stop-heavy configs: in the engine, stop-loss exits realise about 2% worse than the harness's next-point fill (+200 bps calibrated), and the +50 stress does not cover that. Prefer exits that do not fire right after an adverse move, or confirm stops with a second quote before selling.

For signal entries in fee ≤50 pools, assume the real buy price is about 0.35–0.50% above the DexScreener price the harness uses. Momentum entries in the cost-first universe need more than 1.2% expected edge per round trip before they beat booked costs.

Do not deploy any strategy with EXIT_IMPACT_EMERGENCY V1 on fee ≤50 pools. It closed 83% of those trades within about 44 s on quote noise. Use the sell-anchored, arm-then-confirm V2 (the cost-first profile already does). Do not compare Jupiter's priceImpactPct to a 0.75% floor: it includes the pool fee.

Leave the fee-tier table and the 2N/L impact formula unchanged; real quotes confirm them to about 0.1%. Do not lower harness costs for fee 100–125 pools on this thin evidence, which is why the conservative floor is kept.

To extend the calibration, collect more fresh-price evidence. For each quote, log the DexScreener price and its age next to the quote, especially for pools with fee 55–125, liquidity <$50k, and stop exits. Today almost all fresh-price evidence comes from one pool.

result.summary:
Read-only forensics. Inputs: obs.sqlite3 (3.12M rows, 2,042 pairs, 22.76 h), the harness series, the tape snapshot (185k swaps), the /state snapshots taken at 10:23, and the Lab ledger copy in release-backup-20261008-101156. Code read at the deployed commit e964804. Nothing in the runtime or the repo was changed; a find after the runs showed no new files under backend. The harness refused to let me write REPORT.md (subagent policy), so the full report content is in these findings.

Bottom line: none of the live rule sets shows positive expectancy after costs, with or without tape-verified flow. I tried 9 configs: 3 families (WE = main, OFA, CF = cost-first) x 3 flow variants (VF = tape-verified, PROXY = DexScreener txns proxy, NONE). From train only I picked 3: WE_PROXY, OFA_VF and CF_PROXY. All 3 have negative mean net50 on both train and holdout, so nothing qualifies as a candidate.

Holdout results (net50):
- **WE_PROXY:** -3.27% on n=9 (2 pairs). Random entries in the same universe: -4.33%.
- **OFA_VF:** -1.29% on n=6 (4 pairs). Random: -9.59%.
- **CF_PROXY (rug-screened):** -3.75% on n=47 (8 pairs, 5.3 trades/hour). Random: -2.82%, so it does worse than random.

**Why main and OFA open nothing:**
- **Too few candidates.** Main's market rules plus its 1.5% round-trip cap leave 0.14 pools per minute. Only COST_EFFICIENT_FLOW can ever pass the cap. Since 09:00 today the number is 0. OFA has 0.8 pools/min after its 2.75% cap.
- **Tape seats go to the wrong pools.** There are 4 seats (NEO_TAPE_MAX_PAIRS=4). 87.5% of seat time watched pools that no running engine could trade.
- **No free seats right now.** At 10:23 all 4 seats were pinned by held positions: the Lab's VSOF and the cost-first account's WOSE/GOIF/SARP. Entry capacity is therefore 0.
- **Flow often missing even when seated.** 42% of the time a seated pool had no verified flow (DEGRADED).

**Why every close was swordinu:** it was the only pool that met all of these at once:
- matched by COST_EFFICIENT_FLOW;
- in the 30 bps fee tier, with a quoted round trip of about 1.0-1.2%;
- given seat priority by the scheduler as the most persistent pool in the "feasible" group;
- steady buy flow.

All three accounts ran the same rule on the same feed and tape. With a 20-minute cooldown and no memory of losses, they re-bought it every 30-40 minutes while it fell 76%.

**Verified flow vs DexScreener proxy:** verified flow gives a small, short-lived timing signal: +1.51 pp at 5 minutes within the same pool (CI95 +0.62 to +2.54), and about 0 at 15-30 minutes. The DexScreener proxy gives nothing. Neither covers costs.

**URGENT:** the cost-first account opened 3 positions within 80 seconds of going live, and all 3 belong to the serial rug family. The cost-first universe structurally favours this family, because the fee tier is computed from market cap.

- GOIF: $193.7M, 0.65%, 375 min, 2 other pools.
- SARP: $82.6M, 0.99%, 709 min, 4 other pools.
The established drain hazard for this family is about 6% per hour per position. The Lab books MOMENTUM, COST_FIRST_CONTROL and COST_FIRST_SCALED hold VSOF (AGZjpu5v, since 09:52). VSOF is flagged only because its ticker is reused (liquidity/mcap 3.2%, 4.5 days old). These four pools also occupy all 4 tape seats.

findings.title: The cost-first universe structurally selects the fake-market-cap rug family
findings.detail: cost_first_established.rejections works out the PumpSwap fee tier from market cap in SOL, and it has no liquidity/mcap or ticker-reuse check. An inflated fake market cap therefore earns the cheapest tier (30 bps) and passes the 'cheap' screen. Over 22.8 h, 50 of the 61 pools that ever passed the universe are flagged by the interim rug screen; that is 10,986 of 15,911 (69%) universe minute-units. COST_EFFICIENT_FLOW (liquidity/mcap >= 1.5%) and OFA (>= 3%) do have a liquidity/mcap floor; the cost-first universe removed it.

findings.title: Main engine: market rules x 1.5% cost cap leave about zero candidates
findings.detail:
Funnel (forensics/funnel.py) applies the engine's own rule functions to each obs row. Each unit is a (minute, pool) pair; main scans about 20 times a minute.
- Feed: 77.5 pools/min.
- PumpSwap + SOL quote: 55.0.
- Any WINNER_ENSEMBLE market rule: 6.49.
- Cost <= 1.5% round trip: 0.144 (in 14.1% of minutes).
- Verified flow present: 0.115.
- Fresh: 0.113.
- Promoted buy pressure: 0.078.
- Rule flow match: 0.078 (7.8% of minutes).

Only COST_EFFICIENT_FLOW ever produced a cost-feasible unit (187 of 187). EARLY, MOMENTUM, PRECISION, ULTRA_PRECISION and VERIFIED_FLOW_MOMENTUM target young pools in the 100-125 bps tiers, with round trips of 2.4% or more, so they can never pass. Only 5 distinct pools passed all non-flow rules in 22.8 h: swordinu 155 units (83%), Agency 18, neet 9, CATE 3, IOF 2. Since 09:00 today there are zero.

Check against the engine's own rejection names: 1,782,324 winner_signal rows agree with the reconstruction, 11,153 (0.6%) disagree.

Snapshot at 10:23: 82 winner_signal and 8 promoted_verified_flow_unavailable. Of those 8, 7 fail on fees alone; EVERYTHING (52 bps tier) is feasible but has no seat.

findings.title: Tape seats: 4 total, mostly spent on untradable pools, and 0 free right now
findings.detail:
Live start script: NEO_TAPE_MAX_PAIRS=4. Live tape status at 10:23: pinned_exit_pools=4, entry_capacity=0.

Over 22.8 h (forensics/seatuse.py), 7,387 (minute, pool) units were on the tape:
- 61.7% were matched by main's rules but over main's cost budget;
- 29.6% were exploration or pins;
- 8.7% were feasible.
- 87.5% of all seat-minutes were on pools that no running engine could trade under its non-flow rules (ECSTASY 565, VSOF 357, SNDWITCH 320, A1 312, ...).

The scheduler ranks seats using only main's rules (winner_ensemble.market_candidates) plus the funded rules and the cost-first universe; it does not know OFA's rules. Share of units that passed every non-flow rule but were blocked only by missing verified flow:
- WE: 20.3%
- OFA: 72.7%
- CF: 96.8% (92.1% after the rug screen)

Verified flow exists in 4.75% of units, on 220 pools, about 3.68 pools at a time (median 4). Pins took on average only 0.84 seats (Lab 3,796 owner-minutes, main 135, 18802 42). They were heavy on 10-07 between 11:00 and 16:00, and are 4 of 4 now.

findings.title: Why every close was on swordinu
findings.detail:
There are 23 closes in the three snapshots: 20 swordinu (69fyvgoT), 1 CRAWL, 1 MISTAKE (+10.15%). All were taken under WINNER_ENSEMBLE_PAPER_V1 and all matched COST_EFFICIENT_FLOW.
1. Three accounts ran the same strategy on the same feed and tape, so entries landed within seconds of each other (for example 00:53:27, 00:53:40, 00:56:19). They were one experiment, not three.
2. swordinu was the only pool that met both the rule and the cost cap: 30 bps tier (market cap $17-22M), liquidity about $450k, score 80-88, older than 1 day, liquidity/mcap 2.2%. Modeled round trip at $200 was 1.18-1.20%; quoted was 0.78-1.23%. The other feasible-group pools (MISTAKE, Agency, CRAWL, e/acc, JEANPHIL, EVERYTHING; 52-70 bps tiers) quote 1.3-1.9% at $200. CRAWL and MISTAKE only got in at $50 via the size backoff.
3. The scheduler gives main-rule-matched, fee-feasible pools (GROUP_FEASIBLE) first claim on seats and lets them pre-empt exploration seats. swordinu held 155 of 684 feasible units, 140 of them on the tape.
4. It had steady buy flow.
5. There is a 20-minute same-token cooldown and no memory of losses: 8,774 cooldown rejections on swordinu, then a re-buy every 30-40 minutes as it fell 76%.

findings.title: Seated pools lose verified flow 42% of the time (DEGRADED)
findings.detail:
forensics/degraded.py sampled 27,669 rows where the pool was on the tape: 57.9% COMPLETE, 42.1% DEGRADED.
- **11.0 pp** of the degraded share is caused by SWAP_ACTOR_NOT_TRANSACTION_SIGNER swaps. These are 1.5-3% of decoded swaps, but market_monitor.live_flow marks the whole 30 s window DEGRADED if a single flagged event falls inside it.
- **31.2 pp** has no flagged event in the snapshot. Likely causes are the 30 s complete_since warm-up after every new 60 s lease and pagination backlog on busy pools (Agency 99.8%, RARI 92%, A1 73%, SNDWITCH 69% degraded).

QUOTE_USD_UNKNOWN made up nearly all events from 10-07 03:00 to 08:00 but is rare after 10-07 17:00.

findings.title: EXIT_IMPACT_EMERGENCY V1 fires as a timer, but the entries were the real problem
findings.detail:
18 of 23 closes were EXIT_IMPACT_EMERGENCY (V1). All 18 had less than 2% liquidity change, and in 12 the market move at exit was 0 or better. The impact of a $200 sell quote on these pools reads 0.75-1.0% (two-hop route token -> SOL -> USDC), which is at or above the 0.75% floor.

Counterfactual: replaying a plain -5/+10/60 net exit from the same 23 entries in the harness gives -2.75% per trade (18 STOP, 5 TP), against -1.73% actually realized. V1 limited the losses; the bad entries (one declining pool) caused them.

Total P&L of the 23 closes: -$94.23, of which EIE exits -$51.41.

findings.title: Main spends the shared quote budget on pools its own model says are infeasible
findings.detail: Rejection rows after the flow gate on 100-125 bps pools (RARINU, CATCRAFT, ZKDARK, A1, ...): 3,858 quote_inconsistent, 4,950 quote_retry_cooldown, 845 roundtrip_cost. entry_quote_priority only moves these pools to the back of the queue; it never drops them. The fee model can overstate cost (CRAWL modeled 1.91% vs quoted 0.88%; MISTAKE 1.71% vs 1.49%), so these pools should be throttled, not dropped.

findings.title: Verified flow vs DexScreener txns proxy (Q3)
findings.detail:
Proxy, fixed before looking at outcomes: b5 >= 3 and b5/max(s5,1) >= 1.2. Sample: one point per pool per minute, rug-screened: 35,636 samples, 1,191 of them on the tape.

- **Selection:** pools on the tape are not better than pools off it in the same fee/liquidity bucket (15 min net): fee<=50 & liq>=250k -2.92 vs -1.38; fee55-95 & >=250k -3.02 vs -2.28; fee100-125 & 50-250k -5.43 vs -3.96.
- **Inside the covered sample:** verified-flow pass vs fail at 15 min: -2.06% vs -3.09%. Within the same pool: +1.51 pp at 5 min (CI95 +0.62 to +2.54, 18 pools, 72% positive), -0.23 pp at 15 min (CI -4.5 to +3.2), -0.67 pp at 30 min.
- **Proxy in the same covered sample:** -1.41 pp at 5 min, -0.09 pp at 15 min. The proxy is on for 88% of covered points, so it barely filters.
- **Uncovered pools:** proxy on vs off within pool at 15 min: mean -9.3 pp, median -0.6 pp (pump-and-dump tails).

recommendations: URGENT (adds a safety rule): put the rug-family screen into cost_first_established.rejections. That one function is used by the cost-first engine profile, both COST_FIRST Lab books and the scheduler's GROUP_COST_FIRST. Reject a pool when: market cap >= $20M with liquidity/mcap < 2% on a token younger than 14 days, or a young token whose ticker already exists on another pool. Separately, the owner should decide what to do with the 3 open rug-family PAPER positions in 18802 (WOSE, GOIF, SARP) and the Lab's VSOF.

Make tape entry seats engine-aware. Rank first the pools that pass the non-flow rules and cost cap of at least one running engine (main WE at 1.5%, OFA at 2.75%, the cost-first universe), after the rug screen; then exploration. Pools matched by main's rules but over every running engine's cost cap go below exploration. Evidence: 87.5% of seat-minutes were on untradable pools; OFA-eligible pools had verified flow only 27% of the time. WE + OFA demand (about 1 pool/min) fits in 4 seats.

Pin a held pool to a tape seat only when the position's exit logic reads exact-pool flow: OFA adaptive exits and Lab MOMENTUM_RUSH_BRAIN. Main's 'fixed' exits, cost_first exits and the other Lab books use no flow, so their pools should drop to a lower observation tier that yields to entry candidates. At 10:23 such pins took all 4 seats, leaving entry capacity at 0. First check that nothing else (dashboards, training) depends on those pins.

Stop discarding a whole 30 s window because of one SWAP_ACTOR_NOT_TRANSACTION_SIGNER swap. Count a confirmed, USD-valued swap conservatively: a SELL counts toward sells; a BUY is excluded from buys and from wallet counts. Keep DEGRADED for unknown USD, unconfirmed swaps, timing or duplicate problems. This recovers about 11 pp of verified-window time on seated pools, and buy-pressure checks can only get stricter. Ship it as a versioned change with a shadow comparison. Also renew a pool's lease while it stays engine-eligible, so it does not repeat the 30 s warm-up every 60 s.
Add per-pool loss memory to each account: escalate the same-token cooldown after consecutive losses on a pool (for example 2 losses -> 6 h). 20 of 23 closes were repeated re-buys of one falling pool.

Use EXIT_IMPACT_EMERGENCY V2 (or log-only) for main and OFA as a correctness fix, not as a P&L fix. V1 fired on 18 of 23 closes with no liquidity change, but plain -5/+10/60 exits from the same entries would have lost more (-2.75% vs -1.73% per trade).
Throttle quote attempts on pools where fees alone exceed the cap: at most one probe per pool per N minutes, rather than dropping them (the model overstated CRAWL's cost by about 1 pp).

Do NOT replace the tape gate with DexScreener proxies, and do NOT raise cost caps to force trades. CF_PROXY traded 5.3 times an hour at -3.75% per trade in holdout, worse than random entries in the same universe; the WE and OFA proxies were negative too.

Tell the owner plainly: no tested configuration has shown positive expectancy, so the changes above remove waste and a toxic universe; they do not create profit. 'Huge incomes' are not supported by this data. Keep each account on a distinct hypothesis and judge them on the STRATEGY_VALIDATION acceptance basis (+50 bps per leg, CI lower bound > 0).

To attribute OFA's missed opportunities (44 minute-units since 01:28, mostly MISTAKE), read 18801's own entry diagnostics or observation log (a backup copy, not the live files). That shows which of the 60 s flow, buyer-count, safety and quote gates rejected them.

key_findings: NO EDGE: no momentum configuration qualifies as a candidate. All 3 train-selected configs lose on holdout at net50: -16.0%, -11.4% and -6.1% per trade. Each one is WORSE than random entries in the same universe with the same exits (-0.9%, -3.6%, -2.6%). Momentum is anti-predictive here, not just too weak.

It is a direction problem, not a cost problem. The pre-cost (gross) price move after the momentum entries was negative on holdout: -11.7%, -6.9% and -1.7% per trade. Cheaper execution would not rescue it.

Train evidence (fixed-horizon forward net %, rug-screened, vanished pairs exit at last price -10% so they are not dropped). In every universe the top quintile of 5-min return, pc5, 10-min return, distance above the 30-min low, v5/(v1h/12) and 5-min buy share has the WORST forward returns. HI30 (fee >=100 bps, liq $30-50k): top-quintile r5m gives -16.1% at 60 min vs a -5.6% base. HI50: -11.6% vs -5.5%. MID (fee 55-95): -5.4% vs -4.0%. LO (fee <=50, liq >=$250k): -0.5% vs +0.5%. In HI30, buy share >0.7 gave -25% at 60 min. Runner coins (pc24 >=100% and pc6h >=0) gave -23.7% (HI30) and -15.6% (HI50) at 60 min.

352 train configs were run through H.simulate: 8 momentum signals x 4 universes x 6 exits (192), plus a trend-pullback refinement and LO-scaled momentum x 5 exits (160). Every pure-momentum config was negative on train at net50, the best being -3.04%/trade. Signals tried: 5-min spike, 30-min trend near its high, 30-min-high breakout, volume acceleration, LO-scaled spike and trend. Exits tried: trailing, let-winners-run up to 180 min, tight 15-30 min, wide stops. None helped. Let-winners-run trailing exits were usually worse than tight time exits.

The only positive train results (trend-pullback in HI30, about 0 to +1.1%/trade) came from ONE trade: LOBBY, pair FkfDrvbz, gapped through a +15% take-profit to +408%. Removing that single pair gives -4.6% to -4.9%. This was visible on train before the holdout run, and the holdout then confirmed the configs fail.

Stops gap through badly after pumps in high-fee pools. Trend-pullback STOP exits averaged -17.4% against a -8% stop level, and 27% were worse than twice the stop. Two holdout trades (BATONPASS BERQeJZD, DIAMONDANT 6B4sAoGv) lost about 98% within one minute of entry, likely dev or holder dumps. Random-entry stops averaged -11.4%, with only 9% beyond twice the stop. Modeled round-trip cost in these pools is 3.5-4.2% (+1.0% under stress): fee about 110 bps per leg, median liquidity $52-77k.

Other momentum variants tested on train all stayed negative: a market-breadth regime filter (cross-sectional median 30-min return), volatility-normalised momentum (z-score of the 5-min return), 'organic' momentum (5-min unique wallets >= 10, low repeat-buy share, tape-verified buy dominance), breakout events (first new 30-min high after 20 min), and LO-scaled thresholds. Tape flow (vf_*) covers only 1-5% of samples and holder data (hp_uw5) 5-30%.

ACTIONABLE: use momentum as a VETO, not an entry. In mid/high-fee pools, skip entries when the 5-min return is >= +3%, the 5-min buy share is >= 0.70, v5/(v1h/12) is >= 1.3, pc6h is >= +200% or pc24 is >= +150%. Out-of-sample support for the veto is indirect: the 3 holdout momentum configs lost to their random baselines by 3.5-15 points. It should be tested directly on data recorded after 2026-10-08 10:27.

key_findings: No F2 config qualifies as a candidate. Buying dips, with or without a stabilisation check, did not beat costs on the holdout, and it did not beat random entries in the same universe either. Do not deploy any F2 config.

Dips do not revert on average. On train, gross forward price returns after a drop of 6% or more matched unconditional returns on the same 35 pools: -0.58% vs -0.37% at 15 min, +0.54% vs +0.60% at 60 min. Stressed (net50) round-trip cost is about 4-5.5% in the fee 100-125 pools and about 2.5% in large fee<=50 pools. Every broad dip bucket therefore lost between -2.6% and -5.8% per trade at net50.

Waiting for stabilisation (selling exhaustion) does not create an edge. In the train event study, entries after the 5-min low was 3 minutes or more old, or after a bounce of 3% or more, did worse than buying at the low, because dead-cat bounces fade. Falling sell counts and the buy/sell ratio did not separate winners from losers. In the two pre-selected holdout pairings, stabilised entries beat the knife by about 1.8 points in both train and holdout, but that gap is far inside the noise (per-trade SD about 20%).

The only positive train pocket was an 'oversold' context: the coin was already down 12% or more over 1 h (or 15% or more over 6 h), then dipped 8-25% below its 15-min high, then stabilised, with wide exits (+20/-25 over 90 min or +25/-30 over 120 min). Its parameter neighbourhood was mostly positive on train (+0.6% to +6.9% mean), but every confidence interval spanned zero, n was 20-44, and the holdout came out -0.26% (config 1) and -4.34% (config 2).

Random entries restricted to coins already down 12% or more over 1 h beat random entries over the whole liq>=50k universe in both splits (6-salt averages: train -1.09% vs -2.46%, holdout +0.20% vs -4.85%), yet still had no positive expectancy at net50. This came from the baselines, not from a pre-registered config, so it is a hypothesis to test on new data, not an edge.

Anti-signal, train only and not validated on holdout: crashes in progress keep falling. With a 15-min drawdown of 25% or worse, the gross forward return was -14.6% at 15 min and -16.9% at 30 min (13 pairs). A 5-min drop of 20% or worse continued -11.7% over 15 min. Other families should forward-test a hard veto on entries in that state.
Anti-signal, train only: pullbacks in coins that already ran hard keep falling. Buying a stabilised 10-22% dip in a coin up 50% or more over 6 h lost -10% to -18% per trade at net50 (10 pairs).

Exit shape matters a lot under these costs. Wide brackets (+20/-25) cut the cost drag sharply compared with -5/+10. Random entries over the liq>=50k universe were -0.49% on train with +20/-25/90 (versus -7.7% for the established -5/+10/60 all-PumpSwap baseline), but -5.39% on the holdout. Holding for 60 min with no stop or target was clearly worse (-9.2% on train for mid-depth dips).

Most of the holdout losses came from coins in organic collapse, which the interim rug screen does not catch: swordinu stopped out at -28% to -41% as its fee tier slid from 30 to 55 bps, and TON618 stopped at -26% to -32%. The screen also flags legitimate copycat tickers (CLAUDIA, TWEETCRAFT, Agency). A slow-collapse guard is needed (for example a falling fee tier or market cap, or pc6h at or below -40%).

The universe is too thin for this family. Only about 35 clean PumpSwap pools with liquidity of $50k or more had any dip in the 13.7 h train window; big low-fee pools almost never dip (3-5 pairs). With win rates near 50% and payoffs of plus or minus 20-30%, 30 trades give a 95% CI of roughly plus or minus 9% per trade, so at least 7 days of data are needed before mean reversion can be judged.

key_findings: Verdict: no edge, and nothing qualifies as a candidate. I tried 38 configurations on train and froze 3. On holdout each made only 3 trades on 3 pairs: Gitretriever, B22 and LOADED, all STOP exits at -25 to -28% net50. Holdout means: -26.7%, -28.5% and -26.7%. Random entries in the same universe on holdout, pooled over 10 salts: -32.2% (24 h universe, E1), -32.0% (E2), -17.8% (2 h universe).

The data can barely see new pools. 1,423 PumpSwap pools were first seen younger than 60 min (about 57 graduates per hour, almost all from gecko-new-pools). The median pool was observed for only 1.0 min (11 points), and only 48 were observed for 60 min or more. 91% left the feed within 15 min and 97% within 60 min. The tape does not help: 1 of 228 young tape pools has events after its last scan point. So entering at graduation cannot be backtested honestly; such trades close VANISHED on the assumed -10% haircut.

Kaplan-Meier survival, where death means price below 50% or liquidity below 20% of the reference. For pools in the feed at least 10 min and younger than 4 h (n=162): 76% survive at 15 min, 51% at 60 min, 41% at 120 min, 25% at 240 min. Only 7% doubled within 60 min. The subset that passes the interim rug screen (n=58): 59% survive at 60 min and 54% at 120 min, and only 2% doubled within 60 min. First-sight graduates (n=1273, heavily censored): 29% survive at 60 min and 2% were seen to double. Fat tails are rare; halving is common.

Forward 60-min returns on train samples (net50, $100) are negative in every age bucket. Means: -39.5% for age 3-15 min, -32.2% for 15-30, -20.7% for 30-60, -24.7% for 60-120, -17.4% for 120-240, -10.1% for 4-24 h. Exiting at the last observed point with no vanish haircut still gives -19.7% (age 15-60) and -17.9% (age 60-240).

Cost floor: a $100 trade in a typical $20k graduate costs about 4.7% round trip on the net50 basis (fees of 115-125 bps per leg, 1% impact per leg, buffers and stress), so every trade starts at about -4.7%. A -15% stop in these thin pools typically fills at -17 to -28% because the price gaps through it.

The organic-growth signal (liq and price both up at least 10% over 15 min, 5 or more unique buyers in 5 min, buy share 50-80%) was the only idea not clearly negative on train. In the 24 h universe it made +4.5% (n=23, 11 pairs) against -3.0% for random entries, but its CI of the mean $ was [-13.8, +26.2]. On holdout it failed.
Breakout configs (pc1h >= 20, b5 >= 30) and runner-dip configs looked positive on train (+4 to +26%). The gains came only from feed-gap trades: once those are removed the means are -6 to -13%.

Two harness artifacts inflate early-life results; the audited harness should fix both. (1) Exit impact is capped at 20%, so a drained pool still pays 80% of its quoted price. Example: Leoncio (AvUStCR9) printed a 112x price as its liquidity went to 0, and the harness books +7,600%. Uncapped constant-product exits, receiving R*V/(R+V) with R = liq/2, fix it (f3lib.cp_net50). (2) After a feed gap, hold or stop exits fill at the first point after the gap, which can be hours later. Pools come back because they pumped, so this is survivorship. Examples: US (A7cJ8yHX) at +2,080% after a 9.5 h gap, LOBBY (FkfDrvbz) at +414% after 139 min.

There is a second scam family at launch: fake-liquidity pools with liquidity/mcap of 1.5-2.0, $100-250k of liquidity at age < 30 min, and heavy ticker reuse (SharkTank 34 prior pairs, CAPYBARA 28, TWEETCRAFT 13). Several rose 1.4-2.6x and then had their liquidity pulled to 0 (TITS, TWEETCRAFT, BORDR, Anthropic, SharkTank). The fake-mcap family (liquidity/mcap < 0.05) also shows up at first sight. A liquidity/mcap band of [0.15, 0.70] removes both families, and the engine should adopt it.

The holdout is low-powered because coverage shifted. Graduates kept arriving at 70-89 per hour in the later hours, but few stayed in the feed. Qualifying strict-screen pairs dropped from 2-9 per hour in train to 0-4 per hour in holdout. Practical takeaway for the owner: on this evidence the engine should not buy young pools.

Every universe has a negative unconditional mean forward net50 at 30 min on train: low-fee big pools -1.7%, mid-fee -3.9%, high-fee $50-250k -6.1%, high-fee $20-50k -7.3%. A signal must add 2-7 points just to break even.

This holds for va1h > 1.4, tx5 > 238, hp_uw5 > 57, tape unique buyers > 39 and tape first-time buyers > 15. Median 30-min MFE there is 10-15%: these are pumps that dump. Activity predicts the size of a move, not its direction, and long-only that loses after costs. Best use: an avoid / exit input, not an entry trigger (train-only evidence).

The 'breadth beats a few large buyers' hypothesis is contradicted in its raw form. The lowest tape top-buyer-share quintile (many similar-sized buyers, typical of bot swarms) averaged -11.7% at 30 min. Whale-dominated flow (top share > 0.83) was least bad at -1.6%.

Simulated flow entries on train with exits: spike entries -6 to -8% (worse than random at -5.3 to -5.6%). DexScreener broad-buyer entries -2.8 to -5.9%. Established-pool wake-up (va6h >= 3) -2.6 to -4.6%. Tape-flow exits (sell into frenzy, exit on sell pressure) did not lift the trimmed mean above 0.

Tape vs DexScreener: the engine's vf_* covers only 3.3% of PumpSwap points. Rebuilding past-only features from tape_snapshot.sqlite3 (block time <= t and ingest time <= t) makes 19.5% of samples tape-live. C1 (tape breadth with no-chase filter) is the best F5 result, and it is not tradeable evidence. Holdout: +1.28% mean net50, median +5.37%, win 63.6%, PF 1.29, n=22 on 8 pairs, CI95 of mean $ [-3.87, +7.15]. It fails top_pair_share (0.409 > 0.35). Portfolio (3 slots) on holdout: $1000 -> $1035 over about 9 h. Nothing here supports 'huge incomes'.

Costs dominate: the average stressed round trip at entry was about 2.8-3.2% for the C1 trades. Stops gap through, averaging about -14% on a -10% stop in train (fills come at the next point about 5 s later). Sizing at min($200, 0.2% of liquidity) improved % results slightly and consistently on train, so it was adopted for all configs.

Discipline: 2,208 configurations were tried, all on TRAIN. That is 1,200 factor-screen cells (3 universes x 25 factors x 2 directions x K{1,3} x 4 horizons), 720 rotation-simulator configs (3 universes x 2 tick periods x 15 score specs x K x buffer x stop) and 288 more (established-pool universes, max hold on/off, 2 market gates). The 3 configs were picked by a rule fixed in advance; the holdout ran once (final_eval.py).

Structural cost wall: the rug-screened liq >= $50k PumpSwap universe has a median of only 16 pools per tick. Its average modeled round trip at $200 is 2.1-2.5%, and the average pool drifts down even before costs (approx gross -0.6% / -1.4% at 15 / 60 min on train; -0.15% / -0.7% on holdout). A random pick therefore returns -3.2% to -4.8% net50 per trade.

In the train factor screen, no factor's top-K had a positive mean net50 at any horizon (5-60 min) in any universe. The best was the 3 largest pools in U100 at 60 min: -0.12% (excess over the universe +4.3%, mostly lower cost and less decay).

Momentum and flow factors were the WORST picks after costs: 5-min change, 15-min return, volume acceleration, 15-min liquidity growth, 5-min buyer share, unique 5-min wallets. They averaged -4% to -8% per trade across mechanics. Buying the hottest pools in the cross-section is the opposite of an edge here; size, low volatility and 6h reversal were merely the least bad.

A -8% net stop hurt every factor: shake-outs, with fills around -9.4% after gap-through. Market-level gates (breadth of 15-min returns, median 1h change) also hurt (avg -2.5 / -3.4 vs -0.7 without a gate) because gate flicker forces full round trips. Longer holds with hysteresis were least bad, since costs are paid less often.

Controls: random-K rotation with identical mechanics averaged -3.0 to -3.3% per trade on holdout. At 5-min rebalancing it made ~23 trades/hour and took a 3-slot $1000 portfolio to $133 in 9 h. Fast rotation is a cost machine.

Matched-random controls (same count, ticks and horizon; 5 salts) averaged -4.12 / -6.37 / -5.14% on holdout. The reversal and size configs beat them on average but stayed clearly negative, and the CIs are wide ([-20, +7] $/trade for reversal).

Even large, old pools crashed inside the window: CATE (HMzvsEEm, 73 days old, $3.5M liquidity, 30 bps fee) fell about 30% within an hour roughly 2 h after the cut. That was a price crash, not a liquidity drain, so no rug screen could catch it. swordinu (69fyvgoT) fell -72% and e/acc (4JAnKFdd) bled -41% during holdout.

Train gains were luck from the regime: approximate gross per trade was +4.1 to +5.1% on train (a rally in the second half of train) and -0.6 to -8.0% on holdout. The selected train means (+0.8 to +1.6%) sit in the upper tail of a grid whose average was about -2 to -3.5%.

Practical implication for the owner: periodic cross-sectional rotation should NOT be deployed. In this data, the levers that reduce losses are all cost levers: fewer trades, bigger and lower-fee pools, longer holds, no tight stops, no chasing heat. None of them produces positive expectancy, and nothing here supports 'huge incomes'.

synthesis.headline:
VERDICT: nothing in the recorded data makes money after realistic costs, so 'huge incomes' are not supported.

**Leaderboard result**
- 0 configurations pass the candidate gate. That covers 27 family configs (picked from 65,093 train evaluations), 3 replays of the live rule sets and 2 live cost-first rules, all run on the audited harness at calibrated stressed cost.
- The #1 row is a random-entry baseline that drew lucky (99th percentile of 400 random seeds).
- The best real config is F5 tape breadth: +3.05%/trade on only 11 trades. Four independent verifiers refuted it.

**Forward check on fresh data**
I froze the tests and hashed them before reading the 1.92 h logged after the dataset ended (07:26-09:21 UTC, 92,654 points, 290 pairs), then ran them once. Every tested way of entering still lost:
- The live cost-first rule lost -1.92%/trade (n=36, 18 pairs, 34 of 36 losers, CI95 below 0).
- Random entries lost -7.1% to -8.0%/trade.
- In the biggest low-fee pools, a 30-min hold lost about 2.3% on average after stressed costs. Even the best 10% of those windows still lost at least 1.2%, because the price barely moves while every round trip pays the fee.

**What the evidence does support (defensive only)**
1. **A structural rug guard.** In pools that ever held $250k or more, every one of the 19 drains came from two scam families: pools where liquidity is at least as large as market cap, so the creator can pull it ('LP-pullable'), and pools showing a huge market cap on thin liquidity ('fake market cap'). Forward check: flagged pools lost 50% or more within 60 min 10.8% of the time, against 1.7% for pools that passed.
2. **A heat-veto stack.** Pre-registered forward test: entries the veto would block averaged -8.7% at 30 min, against -3.7% for kept entries (CI below 0).

**Why the engines behave this way**
- **Main and OFA take no trades.** Their cost caps leave almost no eligible pools, and all 4 tape seats are pinned by held positions.
- **The cost-first account and the Lab lose.** 69% of the cost-first universe is the fake-market-cap scam family, and the live rule does worse than random entries in that universe.

**Plan**
1. Stop the structural losses today.
2. Fix the plumbing.
3. Forward-test 3 pre-registered Lab hypotheses for 3-7 days under a strict promotion gate.

evidence_backed.spec:
A pure pre-entry rule that fails closed.

**Where it runs:** before quoting, before flow promotion and before the RugCheck call. It goes in backend/cost_first_established.rejections, the one place shared by the cost-first engine profile, both COST_FIRST Lab books and the scheduler's GROUP_COST_FIRST, and in every other entry path.

**Inputs:** liquidityUsd, marketCap (fall back to fdv), and pair age from pairCreatedAt.

**Reasons recorded in describe()**, checked in this order:
1. rug_input_unknown: any input missing, non-finite or <= 0. Stop here.
2. rug_lp_pullable: liq/mcap >= 1.0.
3. rug_young_pool: age < 720 min.
4. rug_fake_market_cap: mcap >= $20M AND liq/mcap < 1% AND age < 14 days.

**Recommended conservative additions.** Blocking more costs nothing in expectation because no strategy has an edge.
- Raise the fake-market-cap liq/mcap threshold to 2%. This catches DAWS-like pools; it was informed by the holdout and is not validated.
- Use a corrected ticker-reuse rule. Block a token younger than 14 days whose normalized ticker was already seen on another pair with a DIFFERENT mint. The interim rule counts a token's own pump.fun curve pair as a reuse, which is wrong.

**Naming:** call it something distinct from engine_rug_guard.py's RUG_GUARD_V2. That RugCheck-based check never ran on these families (checked_at 0) and passed SharkTank, which later collapsed.

**Companion fix:** in market_monitor.score_pair, limit the +9 'good liquidity/MC' bonus to 0.15 <= liq/MC < 0.6 and treat liq/MC >= 1 as a risk. Today, pools whose creator can pull the liquidity score 86.7 on average and sit at SETUP on 96.9% of rows.

- **Honest caveat:** in this 1.9 h window no fake-market-cap pool drained. The cost-first trades the guard removed actually did better (-1.1% vs -2.7%) because the scam pools drift up on wash buys until they are drained. The guard's value is in the drain tail, about -100% per event (10 of the 64 pools that entered the cost-first universe drained within 22.8 h), and a 2-hour window cannot show that.

evidence_backed.name: HEAT_VETO_STACK: a defensive entry filter
evidence_backed.spec:
Block a new entry in every book, and log the reason, when any of these holds at decision time. All inputs are fields the engine already has.

- (a) 5-min price return >= +3%, measured against the price 300 s earlier.
- (b) DexScreener 5-min buy share b5/(b5+s5) >= 0.70.
- (c) Volume acceleration v5/(v1h/12) >= 1.3.
- (d) pc6h >= +200% or pc24 >= +150%.
- (e) Fee tier >= 100 bps and the pair carried the paid-profile 'latest' flag (token-profiles/latest) at any point in the last 60 min.
- (f) Price <= 75% of its 15-min high, or 5-min return <= -20% (a crash in progress).
- (g) Turnover v5/liquidity >= 0.095 (the 80th percentile on pre-cutoff data).

Optional exit trigger, to run log-only first: sell a held token when it makes its first paid-profile appearance.

Lab arms that test a surge hypothesis (LAB_A) log these flags but do not apply them.

**Where the rules come from:**

synthesis.honest_expectations:
**Short answer for the owner:** nothing recorded so far shows a way of trading these pools that makes money after realistic costs. 'Huge incomes' cannot be promised, and any dashboard showing them should be distrusted; the most likely cause would be a fill artifact. Everything here is PAPER money.

**Why it loses**
- Every trade pays a round-trip cost: about 2% in big low-fee pools, and 4-6% in the 100-125 bps pools where prices actually move.
- In the 1.92-hour forward window, the biggest low-fee pools barely moved. A 30-minute hold lost 2.3% on average after stressed costs, and even the best 10% of those windows lost at least 1.2%.
- The volatile pools lost about -8% at 30 minutes and carry the drain risk.
- Nine families of signals were tested: momentum, dips, new pools, paid attention, order flow, whales, rotation, market regime and exit tuning. None picks winners well enough to cover those costs. The best ones are only slightly better than random entries and still lose.

**Why the four strategies behave as they do**
- **Main and OFA take no trades.** Their own cost caps leave about 0.1 eligible pools per minute. In 22.8 hours only 5 pools ever passed main's 1.5% cap, and swordinu was 83% of those. All 4 tape seats were pinned by held positions, and 42% of watched windows were DEGRADED. Forcing them to trade would only add losing trades.
- **The cost-first account and the Lab lose.** Their universe is mostly a serial scam family whose fake market caps earn the cheapest fee tier. The rule enters whatever is eligible and pays costs on pools that barely move: forward -1.9%/trade, 34 of 36 trades losing.
- **A 15-minute loss tells you nothing.** One trade's result typically varies by 9-13%, so even a real edge needs hundreds of trades to show up.

**What realistic success would look like**
- After about a week of disciplined Lab testing, one hypothesis might show +0.5% to +2% per trade with a confidence interval above zero. At $200 per trade and 3 slots, that is on the order of tens of dollars a day on a $1000 PAPER book, with 10-30% drawdowns along the way.
- Proving even +1% per trade needs roughly 1,000-3,200 trades, which is weeks at these rates.
- The most likely outcome is that all three Lab hypotheses come back negative. That is still worth knowing.
- Until then, the only changes with evidence that they reduce losses are defensive: the rug guard, the heat veto, fewer and cheaper trades, and no tight stops in expensive pools.

**Thinking outside the box**
- The single strongest directional signal in the whole study is bearish: paid DexScreener promotion comes before a -45% to -51% median move. Long-only PumpSwap trading cannot short it, so its use is as a veto and an exit trigger.
- Real memecoin profits come from things this engine cannot do at a 5-30 second polling latency: same-block sniping, MEV, and cross-pool arbitrage. Market making (providing liquidity) is not modelled here, and in coins that fall 50-76% impermanent loss would dominate.

**Caveats**
- The study covers 22.8 hours in one market regime, and the forward window is only 1.92 hours (07:26-09:21 UTC). The forward check confirms directions, not magnitudes.
- I did not write FINAL_REPORT.md: subagents are blocked from writing report .md files. This output is the report.
- I did not read any live ledger. Positions are described from DexScreener prices only.
- Nothing in the runtime or the repository was changed, and no process was stopped.
